 Order

11.05.2023 Heard Mr. G.N. Sahewalla, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner assisted by Ms. K.
Bhattacharya.

Also heard Mr. A.C. Sarma, learned Senior Counsel for the respondent No. 5 assisted by Mr. G. Bharadwaj, Mr. M. Chetia, learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 2, 3 & 4 and Ms. G.
Hazarika, learned counsel for the respondent No. 1.
2.

The petitioner's case is that he is the owner of land measuring 1 Bigha - 1 Katha - 4 Lechas covered by Dag No. 187 of K.P Patta No. 202, Village- Abhaypur, Mouza-Sila Senduri Ghopa under North Guwahati Revenue Circle of Sub-Division-Kamrup Sadar, District-Kamrup.

3. The petitioner's counsel submits that the land of the petitioner has been acquired under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Page No.# 3/6 Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 (herein after referred to as the "2013 Act").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He submits that the respondent No. 5, who is the illegal occupier of the petitioner's land is claiming Zirat compensation which should be given to the petitioner.

He submits that if there is a dispute with regard to the apportionment of the Zirat compensation or any part thereof, the Collector has to refer the dispute to the Authority in terms of Section 76 of the 2013 Act.

The counsel for the petitioner accordingly prays that the Collector may be directed to refer the dispute between the petitioner and the respondent No. 5 regarding the Zirat compensation, to the Authority in terms of Section 76 read with Section 51 of the 2013 Act.
4. Mr. A.C. Sarma, learned Senior Counsel for the respondent No. 5 submits that he has got no objection to the prayer made by the petitioner's counsel.

He however submits that in terms of the judgment of this Court in Arun Ch. Baruah & Anr v. State of Assam & Ors. reported in 2021 4 GLT 974, the Zirat compensation should be paid to the occupier of the land, i.e. the respondent No. 5.

entities.text: Arun Ch. Baruah & Anr v. State of Assam & Ors. reported in 2021 4 GLT 974
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He also submits that the respondent No. 5 is the bonafide occupier of the land and the RCC building,

sentences.text:
5. The counsels for the State respondents submit that the matter may be referred to the Authority in terms of Section 76 read with Section 51 of the 2013 Page No.# 4/6 Act.
6.

In view of the consent of the parties, the letter dated 12.01.2022, issued by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner, Kamrup, Amingaon, directing the Circle Officer, North Guwahati Revenue Circle to make a detailed report of the Zirat compensation, payable to either the petitioner or the respondent No. 5, should not be acted upon by the Circle Officer or the respondent Nos. 2 & 3.
The same may however be sent to the Authority constituted under Section 51 of the 2013 Act.
The respondent No. 2 shall accordingly refer the dispute between the petitioner and the respondent No. 5 to the Authority constituted under Section 51 of the 2013 Act.

7. The Notification No. RLA.300/2013/Pt.II/176 dated 27.05.2020 issued by the Addl. Chief Secretary to the Govt. of Assam, Revenue & D.M. Department, shows that the Authority that has been constituted to decide disputes under Section 76 of the 2013 Act.

The contents of the Notification dated 27.05.2020, issued by the Addl. Chief Secretary to the Govt. of Assam, Revenue &
D.M. Department is reproduced below:
"GOVT. OF ASSAM REVENUE & DISASTER MANAGEMENT (LR) DEPARTMENT A S S A M S E C R E T A R I A T ( C I V I L ) , D I S P U R G U W A H A T I - 6 No.RLA.300/2013/Pt-II/176 Dated Dispur, the 27th May, 2020 Page No.# 5/6 ORDERS BY THE GOVERNOR NOTIFICATION
